newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis sharpens risk control on investment funds.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis sharpens risk control on investment funds.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Thursday he wanted to sharpen risk controls on investment funds and limit the percentage of capital these funds could invest in paper of the same issuer.

"I have decided to cancel the derogation to rules on the spreading of risks introduced in 1991 ... allowing (funds) to hold 25 percent of their assets instead of 10 percent in paper of the same issuer," he said.
"The possibility of derogation has in fact proved to be, in practice, potentially dangerous," he said in a speech.
He said the derogation would be cancelled and the limits would be progressively sharpened, staring with 17.5 percent on January 1, 1997.
Arthuis gave a speech at the award ceremony of the "golden basket" for the best French fund managers.

The Finance Minsiter said that while he was promoting more pension investment funds in France, he was particularly in favour of those funds that would pay out an amount yearly after retirement over funds that ended with a lump-sum capital.
